title.narrative: Emergency response to the most affected by armed conflict in Uvira territory

description.narrative: The problem of armed and intercommunal conflicts in the province of South Kivu remains very complex. Thus, while the territories of Uvira and Fizi were already torn apart by particularly virulent intercommunal and armed conflicts since January 2024, the situation deteriorated further following the capture of the capital of North Kivu province (Goma) by the M23 rebels at the end of January 2025. The capture of Bukavu had an impact beyond the city, particularly in the south of South Kivu province, notably in the territories of Fizi and Uvira, particularly in the large area of Kamanyola in the Walungu territory, bordering Uvira. It should be noted that the renewed fighting occurred only days after US President Donald J. Trump hosted the signing of the Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity between the DRC and Rwanda on 4 December. According to media reports, members of the armed group M23 entered the key city of Uvira on Wednesday 10th December 2025 and residents described a sense of fear and uncertainty. Most of the displaced inside South Kivu are sheltering in overcrowded sites, facing heightened protection risks, poor sanitation and the growing threat of disease outbreaks. Displaced women and girls face heightened risks of gender-based violence in overcrowded shelters. An estimated 500,000 people have fled the fighting, including more than 50,000 individuals who crossed into Burundi before the border was closed. These IDPs are sheltered in different locations as stated by OCHA in the respective alerts: Baraka https://ehtools.org/alert-view/6239 , Mboko https://ehtools.org/alert-view/6238 , Ruzizi health zone https://ehtools.org/alert-view/6227, Sange https://ehtools.org/alert-view/6217 , Kigoma centre https://ehtools.org/alert-view/6214
